$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: The Note Under the Ice

plate.narration: A fold in the air shivers at the end of the passage. Salt wind slips through, though the glacier lies all around. A low note trembles under the rock. Something here is waiting for an answer.

goal.text: Search the glacier for another opening.

steps.label: Follow the herd's ears to the ridge
Find what is making the ticking
Decide what to do about it

search.narration: You stay near the singing hall instead of taking the shelf path. Your job today is to search the glacier for another opening. The seam you tested is still sealed, and it only answers your song. The yeti herder waits at the door with the kid goat under one arm. "My herd keeps stopping at the east ridge," she says. "Ears up, all pointing one way. Something up there ticks. Find it before a goat does."

choices.label: Ask the herder where to start
Walk straight back to the fold

variants.text: You step out of the fold into cold glacier air, in the narrow passage behind the singing hall. The opening stays awake behind you. Out in the snow, the herder waves with the kid goat under one arm. You can walk straight back to the fold, or search the glacier again with her.

back_at_fold.narration: You follow your old marks back along the passage. The cairn is still there, and the fold waits, wide and steady, with salt wind on your cheeks. Nothing about it has changed, except that you know it better now.

plan.narration: The herder points at the east ridge. "Snow is soft up there. Haul the sled, or go light?" Her sled waits by the door with a coil of rope and a lantern tied on. The kid goat has already started chewing the rope. Beside the door, the hay pile is shorter than it was yesterday, and she keeps glancing at it.

choices.label: Load the sled and haul it up
Go light with just the rope and lantern

plan_a.narration: You stack the rope, the lantern and a bundle of hay on the sled. The kid climbs on top of the hay and will not get off. The runners squeak like mice. "Every hand on the rope," says the herder. "Hay is heavy when it has opinions."

plan_b.narration: You tie the lantern to your belt and loop the rope across your chest. The kid trots ahead, delighted. The snow squeaks under your boots. "Keep moving," says the herder. "The crust only holds you if you do not stop."

climb_a.prompt: Every hand on the rope! Haul the loaded sled up the soft slope, step by step.

climb_b.prompt: Everyone scramble up the crust without stopping. Light feet, no pauses!

climb_done.narration: At the top, the wind falls quiet, as if it is listening too. A line of goats stands along the ridge with their ears pointed west, toward the hall. The kid trots over and points its ears the same way. It looks very serious about it.

choices.label: Look at what the goats are facing

climb_slip.narration: The crust cracks and you slide back a few steps. The kid bleats with laughter. The herder hauls you up by the rope, and you reach the ridge with snow in your boots. A line of goats stands there with their ears pointed west, toward the hall. The kid joins them and does the same.

choices.label: Look at what the goats are facing

ridge.narration: The ridge is bare ice and wind. A dark hole the size of a bucket breathes out a cold, hooting draft. Beyond it, the goats stare at nothing at all. "A goat once fell asleep in that hole," says the herder. "He still brags about it." Tick. Tick. Tick. Something is ticking, very faintly. Is the hole the answer?

choices.label: Lie flat and listen along the ice
Walk the ridge and test each draft
Ring the Listening Chime over the hole

ridge_a.prompt: Lie flat with an ear to the ice. Follow the ticking to where it is loudest. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

ridge_b.prompt: Walk the ridge and test every draft with a wet finger. Be quick, the wind keeps changing! Choose who leads; everyone can help.

ridge_chime.narration: You ring the chime over the hole. One clear note rings out. It does not go sour, and it does not echo. "Away from a rift, a very small bell," you remember Orin saying. The hole is only wind in a tube of ice.

ridge_done.narration: The hole only hoots. But the ticking is louder to the west, back toward the hall, and low down, as if it were coming up through the ice from far below. The goats turn their ears that way. You pack snow around the hole so no goat can nose inside. "One place the herd can stop worrying about," says the herder. She sounds relieved, and then worried again.

ridge_off.narration: The wind swings around, and the hole hoots at you rudely. You lose the trail for a while. Then the kid sits down in the one spot where the ticking is loudest, just to see what happens. West, and low down. You pack snow around the hole so no goat can nose inside.

holes.narration: West of the hole, three snow mounds lie in a row, and the ticking seems to jump between them. The kid is sure it knows. It dives into one mound, wiggles, and pops out of another with a snowy nose, then dives again. The herder squints. "Watch the tail. Where does it end up?"

interaction.cue: Watch the kid dive between the mounds, then pick where it ends up.

onSuccess.narration: You dig out the right mound, and there is the kid with its ear pressed to a patch of ice that ticks. West and low, again. The kid sneezes snow on your boots.

onFailure.narration: You dig out an empty mound. The kid pops out of the next one, delighted, and sits on the loudest patch of ice to help. West and low, it ticks.

onAssisted.narration: The herder holds the kid still long enough for you to see it settle by the loudest patch of ice. West and low, it ticks.

kid.narration: A gust shoves the kid sideways. It slides on its belly toward a thin crust of ice over a melt pool. The herder is far too heavy to follow onto that ice. "Kid!" she calls. The kid does not care. It is having the best day of its life. How will you stop it?

choices.label: Throw the rope loop over its horns
Call it back with the low hall note

kid_a.prompt: Throw the rope loop over the kid's horns. The steadiest arm should throw!

kid_b.prompt: Sing the low hall note across the ice so the kid turns toward you. The steadiest voice should lead!

kid_wing.narration: A winged friend leaps into the wind. The wind carries them over the thin crust in a long, easy glide. The rest of you keep the rope clear and ready. The hero who is best at catching can lead; nobody needs to pretend they flew.

kid_wing_check.prompt: A winged hero glides over the thin ice. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

kid_done.narration: The kid pops into your arms, warm and wriggling, and licks your chin with a very cold tongue. "That is a good kid," says the herder. "That is a terrible kid. Same kid." Behind you, the thin crust finally cracks, and dark water shows where the kid would have been. The herder tucks her own lunch bundle into your pack. "For the climb. Do not tell the kid."

kid_off.narration: You miss. The kid slides into a soft drift and pops out with a snowy beard, completely pleased. The herder fishes it out by one leg, and it sneezes on her. She tucks it inside her coat for the rest of the climb, where it chews her buttons.

crack.narration: West of the ridge, the glacier ends at a long crack. Steam curls out of it. The ticking is louder here, and it comes from below. The air smells like warm wet wool, which makes no sense on a glacier. A narrow bridge of snow crosses the crack. The long way around is safe but slow. "My herd goes around," says the herder. "Your choice."

choices.label: Rope up and cross the snow bridge together
Take the long way around the crack
Fly the rope end across first

crack_a.prompt: Rope up! Everyone steps across the snow bridge in time, light and quick.

crack_b.prompt: Read the cracks and shadows. Pick the safest curve around the steaming crack. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

crack_wing.narration: A winged friend takes the rope end and flies it over the steam. On the far side, they tie it to a rock. The rest of you walk the rope bridge with a hand on the line. The best flier can lead the team; nobody has to pretend they have wings.

crack_wing_check.prompt: A winged hero flies the rope across. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

crack_done.narration: On the far side, the herder counts heads and finds the right number, which she says is her favorite sum. The steam warms your faces and fogs everyone's eyebrows. The ticking is almost under your boots now.

choices.label: Follow the ticking down the slope

crack_slip.narration: The snow gives way. You slide down onto a lower ledge on your bottom. It is warm and steamy and smells like wet wool. The herder lowers a rope and hauls you up, one at a time, grunting. Your pride hurts more than your knee. The ticking is almost under your boots now.

choices.label: Follow the ticking down the slope

post.narration: Under a lip of ice stands an old yeti listening post, a pole with a cup of carved ice on top like a giant ear. The herder pats it. "My grandmother's. She listened here when she was small, and never found out what ticked." She nudges you toward the cup. "Put an ear in and tell me what you hear." The ticking is much louder here, and it has a beat.

choices.label: Hum the hall note into the cup
Count the ticks against your heartbeat

post_a.narration: You hum the low hall note into the cup. The ice hums back, a little flat, and the ticking answers a beat later. The herder's ears go up. "It is listening," she whispers. "Do not stop."

post_b.narration: You press a hand to your chest and count. Tick, tick, then a pause, then tick. The pattern repeats. The kid counts too, with its hoof, and gets it wrong in a very confident way.

post_a_check.narration: You hum into the listening cup while the herder listens. She joins your note, then falls quiet to hear what answers.

post_b_check.narration: You count the ticks together and draw them in the snow. The herder places a claw beside each mark. Her grandmother listened here too.

post_done.narration: The pattern matches the song you learned in the hall. Slow, slow, quick. The ticking is not random. It is the hall note, answered from far below. "Under the hall," says the herder. "Of course it is."

choices.label: Take a breath with the herder

warm.narration: The herder finds a dry hollow and sets out a little stove of warm stones. Tea steams. The kid falls asleep on someone's boots. She looks at the shrinking hay pile, then at the slope. "The ticking comes from under the hall," she says. "If you find where it goes, maybe I find a way to feed my herd. There is a tunnel at the foot of this slope. Too narrow for me. I will go around by the hall's wide back door and meet you. Small folk first." She hangs the lantern on your rope and presses a small jar of glowing moss into your hand. "Mosslight. My grandmother's. For dark places."

tunnel.narration: The tunnel mouth is a low arch of clear ice. Beyond it is dark. Your breath hangs in the lantern light, and the ticking goes on somewhere ahead. Every wall looks the same, and your own footsteps come back to you a moment late, like a shy echo. How will you find your way?

choices.label: Light the lantern and search the walls in sections
Close your eyes and follow the hall note's echo
Open the jar of mosslight and hold it up
Let a starweaver light the frost with starlight

tunnel_a.narration: You hang the lantern on the rope and run the rope along the wall. Each of you takes a stretch of ice to study. Frost makes patterns here. Some look like feathers. One stretch looks like a row of little stitches.

tunnel_b.narration: You line up with a hand on the shoulder in front and close your eyes. You hum the hall note. It comes back from the left, a little louder. Hum again, and it comes back from lower down. The ice hums like a very large, very shy cat.

tunnel_star.narration: A starweaver breathes on the wall, and starlight makes the frost sparkle. The ticking line shows up like a path of tiny stars. The others hold the lantern steady and watch their footing. The best reader of frost can lead.

tunnel_moss.narration: You unscrew the herder's jar. Soft light spills out, and the frost wakes up all along the wall. The ticking line shows as a row of tiny shining stitches. The moss fades as you walk, as if it had only one good evening in it, and you tuck the empty jar away.

tunnel_moss_check.prompt: Follow the shining stitches along the wall. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

tunnel_a_check.prompt: Everyone studies a different stretch of wall. Half of you must spot the line of ticks.

tunnel_b_check.prompt: Everyone hums the hall note together and follows the loudest echo, hand on shoulder.

tunnel_star_check.prompt: Starlight lights the frost. The starweaver assists; choose who leads the team check.

tunnel_done.narration: The ticks run along the wall like stitches, then turn down toward a crack at the tunnel's end. Your lantern light jumps, but the line holds. At the crack, the tunnel shrinks around you. You will have to squeeze.

tunnel_off.narration: The lantern swings, and the frost blurs into feathers and stitches and more feathers. You wander in a slow circle and bump into the same wall twice. The third time, you notice the ticks under your hand. They lead to a crack at the tunnel's end, where the tunnel shrinks around you.

squeeze.narration: The crack is just wide enough for one body at a time, and far too narrow for packs. Through it, the ticking is much louder. Cold air slides out, with a faint smell of salt. Part of the roof looks loose. How will you get through?

choices.label: Chip the crack wider with the rope hooks
Work out an order and pass the packs along
Hold up the loose roof with brace
Slip through first and tie the rope on the far side

squeeze_a.prompt: Chip the crack wider with the rope hooks. The strongest arm should lead!

squeeze_b.prompt: Smallest first, packs on the rope, nobody stuck. Work out the order. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

squeeze_brace.narration: A thornguard plants both feet and holds up the loose roof with brace. The others edge past, one at a time, with the packs on the rope. The strongest helper can lead the careful work; nobody needs to pretend they brought another hero's ability.

squeeze_slip.narration: A duskrunner slides through the crack like a ribbon and ties the rope to a knob of ice on the far side. Then the packs go over the rope, and the others follow. The quickest helper can lead the pulling; nobody needs to pretend they slid.

squeeze_brace_check.prompt: A thornguard holds up the roof. The thornguard assists; choose who leads the team check.

squeeze_slip_check.prompt: A duskrunner ties the rope. The qualified hero assists; choose who leads the team check.

squeeze_done.narration: The crack is wide enough for a person now. As you edge in, small chips of ice pat down from the roof, and the roof gives a long, low creak.

squeeze_off.narration: The crack is only half as wide as you hoped. A bucket of ice chips rains onto your heads, and the roof gives a long, low creak. Everyone has frost eyebrows.

squeeze_hold.narration: The loose roof will not stay up by itself. Somebody has to hold it while somebody else crawls through with the rope. Little pebbles patter on your helmets, and the ticking on the far side is louder than ever.

interaction.cue: Hold the roof while your friend crawls through with the rope.

onSuccess.narration: One by one, you come through. The packs follow on the rope. The last one through leaves a streak of frost on the crack, and laughs when it stings their ear.

onFailure.narration: The roof sheds one more shower of ice chips, and the lantern goes through last, swinging. Nobody is hurt, and everybody is a little more frosty.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge the rope hooks under the roof like two small props. They hold just long enough for everyone to come through.

seam_back.narration: You come out in a small round chamber. One wall is smooth and glossy. It is the back of the sealed seam in the singing hall, and it is warm to the touch. The ticking is here, loud as a heartbeat. You are standing right behind the hall's wall. How will you test it from this side?

choices.label: Hum the hall note softly at the seam
Tap the beat on the seam with a stone

seam_a.narration: You hum the familiar hall note at the back of the seam. The herder listens with you.

seam_b.narration: You tap slow, slow, quick against the seam. Then everyone leaves a little silence for its answer.

seam_done.narration: The seam ticks back at you, quicker. Frost sparkles down the wall in a pattern, over and over, as if it wants you to say it back.

seam_echo.narration: The frost sparkles in a pattern: tick, tock, tock, tick. The seam wants it said back, and you are sure of it. Everyone watches the wall, because everyone sees the sparkles a little differently.

interaction.cue: Watch the frost sparkle, then tap the same pattern.

onSuccess.narration: The seam hums, pleased. A thin line of light draws itself along the ice to a crack in the corner, as narrow as a door left open for a cat. The seam itself stays shut. The crack is where the ticking is going.

onFailure.narration: The seam sulks, then slides a thin line of frost down the wall all by itself, to a crack in the corner as narrow as a door left open for a cat. The seam itself stays shut. The crack is where the ticking is going.

onAssisted.narration: You trace the pattern together on the wall. A thin line of light draws itself along the ice to a crack in the corner, as narrow as a door left open for a cat. The seam itself stays shut.

behind.narration: You slip through the corner crack into a narrow passage that runs behind the singing hall. It is cold, and it smells of salt. Water beads on the rock. Far off, you hear the yetis in the hall holding their low note. Ahead, the ticking stops, and something shimmers. Your ears feel strange without it, like a clock that has just been wound down.

choices.label: Walk to the end of the passage

passage.narration: The passage ends at a fold in the air, quite separate from the hall wall. Beyond its shimmer you smell salt wind and hear gulls. Water beads on the rock beside it. What will you try? The light around the fold is called Riftlight.

choices.label: Study the rock around the fold

chime.narration: You strike the chime. Its note goes sour and does not echo. The way is not ready. You wait for silence and hear a lower note trembling under your feet.

variants.text: The chime answers with a clear note and an echo. The opening is still ready, and the return remains available. Your first song was enough.

read.narration: Your starweaver studies the light while the others see a neutral shimmer. The opening hums faintly back. Nothing steps through it, and no one can name the place beyond.

listen.narration: You put an ear near the rock. Under the gull cries, a low note rises and falls. It matches the one you learned in the hall. The smell of salt comes and goes with it.

look.narration: You study the rock around the fold. Frost lines run toward it like the spokes of a wheel, and every line is ticking. Beside the fold, someone long ago scratched a tally into the stone, one mark for every visit. There are not many marks.

beat.narration: The fold ticks in front of you, steady as a clock. The ticking has a beat, and the beat has an order. Each of you holds a clue. Which taps, in which order, match it?

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then tap the beat in order.
clues: The beat starts with a slow tap.
Two slow taps come before anything else.
A quick tap ends the beat, with no rest.

beat_done.narration: Your taps and the ticking line up: slow, slow, quick. The fold brightens, and the salt wind leans in, as if it likes the sound. A gull cries on the other side, very close, and then goes quiet, as if it is listening too. This is no trick of the ice. The fold is answering the hall note, the same note you sang to the seam.

beat_off.narration: The taps tumble into a clatter, and the fold dims. A puff of cold air knocks the pebbles out of your hands. You stop tapping and listen instead, and still catch the pattern: slow, slow, quick. It is the hall note, answered. The fold brightens again.

cairn.narration: The herder squeezes in from the hall's wide back door, huffing frost, with the kid under her arm and a bit of hay stuck in her fur. She sees the fold, sniffs the salt wind, and takes a big step back. "That," she says, "is where my herd must never wander. Goats go through anything. How do we keep them out?"

choices.label: Stack ice blocks across the passage mouth
String a bell line across the passage mouth

cairn_a.narration: You stack the passage marker with the herder, leaving room for people to pass. She tests the blocks before calling the kid back.

cairn_b.narration: You tie the bells across the passage mouth. The herder checks their height against the kid, who immediately tries to eat one.

cairn_smash.narration: A bigfoot lifts the biggest blocks and settles them with a mighty smash, thump, thump, thump. The others fit the small stones in the gaps. The strongest helper can lead; nobody needs to pretend they smashed.

cairn_smash_check.narration: Your bigfoot sets the broad blocks while friends mark a gap for travelers. The herder checks that a curious goat cannot squeeze through.

cairn_done.narration: The passage mouth is marked. Goats will stay out, and travelers will know to look before they step in. The herder pats the cairn as if it were a friend's head. "There. It can be as strange as it likes, on the other side of that."

herder_say.narration: The herder rubs her chin. "So. The ticking is the hall's note, answered from somewhere else. Maybe your song wakes it. Maybe it only wakes whatever waits on the other side. I cannot tell you which." She looks at the salt wind. "It is your road, not mine. I will keep my herd out of it either way." She presses a few coins from the hall's tin into your hand, and a small warm bead after them. "Keepers' fee. The bead is from my grandmother's string."

choices.label: Share a supper bundle with the hungry herder

herder_share.narration: She eats it in two bites, then looks embarrassed. "The hay is not all that is low," she admits. She gives the kid the crust. The kid looks at you as if you were the best person in the world, and then eats the herder's glove.

footing.narration: Before anyone sings beside the fold, the herder checks the floor with her heel and frowns. Meltwater from the beaded rock has made a slick skin of ice that slopes toward the shimmer. "One wobble and somebody slides in feet first," she says. "That is no door to go through by accident." The kid watches a drip run down the wall with enormous interest. "The hall keeps grit by the back door," she adds. "Two coins a sack."

choices.label: Chip steps into the icy floor
Spread grit and lay a plank walkway
Buy a sack of the hall's grit (2 coins)

footing_a.prompt: Chip small steps into the slick floor, deep enough to grip. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

footing_b.prompt: Pick the safest line for the planks and spread grit where the ice is thinnest. Choose who leads; everyone can help.

footing_buy.narration: A young yeti trots up from the hall with a sack of coarse grit and a sign that says GRIT. The herder pays no attention to the sign. You spread the grit in a wide fan, and it bites into the ice at once. Nobody will slide anywhere they do not mean to go. The kid eats a pinch and regrets it.

footing_done.narration: The floor bites back at your boots now. The herder stamps on the planks, then on the steps, then on the kid's tail by mistake, and everybody apologizes. Nobody will slide anywhere they do not mean to go.

footing_off.narration: A boot skids, and someone sits down hard on the ice with a thump that makes the fold shiver. Everyone laughs, and the herder hauls them upright. You spread the last of the grit more carefully. The floor is rougher than you wanted, but it holds.

decide.narration: You remember how the hall seam answered your song. Here the sound comes from the fold itself, and its beat is the beat of your song. The herder waits by the cairn. You can sing the hall note together and see what the fold does, or leave the opening alone and go back to the hall.

choices.label: Return to the hall and the shelf path

hold.prompt: Everyone sings the low hall note and holds it. Half of you must keep it steady all the way to the end.

sing_wobble.narration: The note wobbles. Frost shakes loose from the ceiling in a glittering shower, right down someone's collar. Then the herder hums the low part from the cairn, deep and slow, and you find your note again. It is not a tidy song. It is enough.

sing.narration: You sing the low note. The ticking steadies. The fold widens, letting salt wind brush your cheeks. When you stop singing, it stays open. You have met its condition; you have not changed its rules.

choices.label: Test the way before stepping through

variants.text: You hum again. The opening stays just as wide. It does not need another note; it has stayed open since your first song.

test_open.narration: The chime answers with a clear note and an echo. The opening is ready, and it offers a way back. On the other side, shallow water ripples around patches of mud. You can cross together or return to camp first.

variants.text: The opening stays wide after your song ends. Salt wind and gull cries continue. You can return to camp for the Listening Chime before trusting the crossing.

ready.narration: You stand together beside the fold, with the passage back to the singing hall behind you and the herder's cairn guarding its mouth. The open air smells of the coast. Nobody knows its name yet.

leave.narration: The herder walks you back to the hall by the wide back door, the kid trotting ahead. The cairn stands guard at the passage mouth. The Cairnstep lead is still yours to follow. You can come back and sing the note later.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
